title: How Much Does a Bathroom Renovation Cost in Toronto? | Muddy York Contracting
description: What drives the cost of a bathroom renovation in Toronto, Etobicoke and Mississauga, and how to read a contractor's quote.
todo: Needs real price ranges from Dylan (e.g. powder room refresh, full gut of a standard bathroom, primary ensuite) before publishing.

drivers.p: Keeping the toilet, tub and vanity where they are is the biggest saving. Moving them means opening floors and walls and re-routing drains to the stack.
Tiled walk-in showers with glass doors, niches and rain heads take more labour and material than a tub with a surround.
Large-format and handmade tile, full-height walls and heated floors all add cost.
Older Toronto homes can hide rotten subfloors, old galvanized pipe or out-of-level framing. A good quote lists these as unknowns up front.

title: How Much Does a Kitchen Renovation Cost in Toronto? | Muddy York Contracting
description: What drives the cost of a kitchen renovation in Toronto, from facelifts to opening up the main floor.
todo: Needs real price ranges from Dylan (facelift, full remodel same layout, open-concept with wall removal).

drivers.p: Repainting cabinets and replacing counters and backsplash costs far less than new cabinets and a new layout.
Opening a kitchen to the dining or living room is common. Non-structural walls are straightforward; structural walls need an engineer, a beam and a permit.
IKEA and stock cabinets, semi-custom and fully custom millwork sit at very different price points.
Pot lights, pendants, new circuits for appliances and panel upgrades all add up.

title: How Much Does a Basement Renovation Cost in Toronto? | Muddy York Contracting
description: What drives the cost of finishing or renovating a basement in Toronto, Etobicoke and Mississauga.
todo: Needs real price ranges from Dylan (finish an unfinished basement, full gut and redo, adding a washroom).

drivers.p: An unfinished basement needs framing, insulation, electrical and drywall. A dated finished basement may need demolition first.
A bathroom adds plumbing, and the cost depends on how close it is to the existing stack.
Resilient channel on the ceiling and Rockwool insulation reduce noise between floors.
Media walls, built-in shelving and kitchenettes add cabinetry and finish carpentry.
